title: Use and build agents on the same foundation.
lead: {name} provides a TypeScript SDK for AI agents and a coding CLI built from the same public components. Build agents into your app or use the CLI in your terminal. Configure a model endpoint, tools, permissions, and sessions for your task.
heroNote: Public packages · Node.js 22.12 or later · Model endpoint required
heroVision: We aim to build agents that can reliably improve the systems they are built on.
proofTitle: Explore the components and run your first query.
proofLead: The agent framework brings together sessions, tools, and permission checks. The coding CLI is a maintained interface built on that framework. You can also use the framework in your own Node.js app.
diagramCaption: A shared TypeScript foundation for an SDK you can embed and a CLI you can run in your terminal.
cliPromptIntro: After configuring a provider and model, enter a prompt:
cliExpectedReply: The selected model returns a text reply. Its wording and quality depend on the model. Before asking about project files, decide whether to trust the workspace.
copyFailed: Copy failed. Select the code to copy it.
exampleNote: This example requires a running OpenAI-compatible server and the ID of a model loaded on it. The local port is an example. tasks.title: Add a query to your app
tasks.body: Install the framework and a provider adapter, then call createQuery from a Node.js script. Use InteractiveSession when your own UI needs a longer conversation.
tasks.needs: You need Node.js 22.12+, a configured provider endpoint, and a model ID. The example on this page uses a running local OpenAI-compatible server.

tasks.title: Ask the coding CLI about a project
tasks.body: Run the CLI and configure a provider and model using a hosted API key or a running local endpoint. Decide whether to trust the workspace before the CLI loads project context.
tasks.needs: You need Node.js 22.12+ and an API key or a running local model server. Provider costs and policies depend on the endpoint you choose.

featuresLead: These capabilities are available in the public SDK packages or the coding CLI built from them. Each card lists the relevant packages, classes, flags, or commands and links to the detailed guide.

models.title: Models and providers
models.body: Choose a model for each task and continue the turn with another model if one fails.

safety.title: Tools and safety
safety.body: Use typed tools and check every call before it runs.

sessions.title: Sessions and execution
sessions.body: Keep work running after you close the terminal, or divide it among agents.

extend.title: Connect and extend
extend.body: Bring in servers, skills, and plugins without forking the runtime.

interfaces.title: Interfaces
interfaces.body: Use the same session from a terminal, script, browser, or protocol.

build.title: Build your own
build.body: Use individual layers directly, or combine them into your own product.

providers.title: Multi-provider adapters
providers.body: Use provider packages for Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, and Gemma. Set baseURL to connect to other OpenAI-compatible endpoints, including gateways, Azure, vLLM, and local servers.

fallback.title: Fallback, effort and advisor
fallback.body: FallbackProvider switches the turn to another model if the primary model is overloaded or fails. In the CLI, you can set model effort for each run and configure an advisor model for the agent to consult.

local.title: Local models
local.body: Configure a provider profile to use Ollama, LM Studio, or another OpenAI-compatible server on your computer or network. You run the model. The tools you enable determine what other data leaves your system.

media.title: Image and video generation
media.body: Use the Gemini provider to generate images and the separate ByteDance (ModelArk) provider to generate video. The video provider cannot serve as an agent's chat model.

tools.title: Validated tools
tools.body: createZodFunctionTool checks model arguments against a zod schema before your function runs. Built-in coding tools cover files, search, shell, web fetch and web search.

permissions.title: Permission modes and rules
permissions.body: Each tool call is checked against deny, ask, and allow rules, then evaluated under one of five permission modes. Some destructive actions are never approved automatically, regardless of the mode.

hooks.title: Lifecycle hooks
hooks.body: Run commands when tool, prompt, or session events occur. PreToolUse can block a call. Other hooks can record logs, support audits, or add context to the next prompt.

sandbox.title: OS sandbox for shell
sandbox.body: Shell commands can run inside bubblewrap on Linux and WSL2 or Seatbelt on macOS, limiting what a command can read, write, or reach on the network.

trust.title: Workspace trust
trust.body: Project instructions such as AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md load only in trusted workspaces. For an untrusted repository, the CLI refuses unattended runs or starts in Restricted mode.

sessions.title: Saved, resumable sessions
sessions.body: Continue, resume, rename, or fork a conversation. Context usage is tracked and compacted automatically. The SDK host chooses and supplies the session store.

daemon.title: Background sessions and daemon
daemon.body: Supervised sessions continue running after you close the terminal. A single workspace daemon provides one runtime for multiple terminals and the desktop app.

subagents.title: Subagents and background tasks
subagents.body: Delegate work to subagents with their own context and tools. Run them in the same process or in child processes, and manage queued and running jobs in one place.

automation.title: Loops, schedules and plans
automation.body: Repeat a prompt at a set interval, or wake the agent later or when command output matches a condition. Keep the session read-only until you approve its plan.

checkpoints.title: Checkpoints, memory and cost
checkpoints.body: Rewind to an edit checkpoint or fork from it. Use opt-in memory to retain approved facts across sessions, inspect context usage, and set a monthly cost limit.

workflows.title: DAG workflows
workflows.body: Use /workflows to turn a description into a workflow with the active model. Save it as JSON in the workspace, validate it, and run it, with the option to run detached.

roundtable.title: Multi-agent roundtables
roundtable.body: Bring independent agents and people into a shared transcript. Choose the turn order, run groups in parallel, and use a Robota session as a participant or selector.

mcp.title: MCP in both directions
mcp.body: After explicit approval, connect to stdio or remote MCP servers, including those that use OAuth sign-in. You can also expose a session as an MCP server over stdio or authenticated HTTP.

skills.title: Skills, commands and agents
skills.body: Define skills and commands in Markdown to make them available as slash commands. Agent definitions describe subagents. The CLI discovers these files in the project and your home directory.

plugins.title: Plugins and marketplaces
plugins.body: Install plugins that bundle skills, hooks, themes and MCP servers. SDK lifecycle plugins cover history, logging, usage, limits, errors, analytics and webhooks.

events.title: External events
events.body: Allow a verified external service to send text events to a running terminal session. View or revoke those permissions from within the session.

terminal.title: Terminal UI
terminal.body: An interactive terminal app with a command menu, prompt history search, rebindable keys, file attachments with @path, and a plain-text screen-reader mode.

print.title: Print mode and goals
print.body: Run a prompt from a script or pipe and receive text, JSON, or streaming JSON. Request output that follows a schema, or let the agent work toward a goal over multiple turns.

gui.title: Browser GUI and desktop app
gui.body: Serve the current workspace GUI on a loopback address and open it in a browser. The desktop app in the repository displays the same GUI through the workspace daemon.

http.title: HTTP and other transports
http.body: Let other services submit turns and receive results as server-sent events, protected by a bearer token or OAuth resource server. WebSocket, HTTP, MCP, and WebRTC transports use the same wire protocol.

devices.title: Devices and remote control
devices.body: Message other running sessions, hand a conversation to another session or device, and link your devices. Pair a browser to control a session together over peer-to-peer WebRTC.

ci.title: CI and GitHub Actions
ci.body: Use print mode in a workflow step to review a pull request or respond to a task. Gate the pipeline on an evals-as-code score.

core.title: Conversation engine
core.body: ConversationAgent runs and streams turns with conversation history, tool calling, structured output, and plugins. The minimum setup is core and one provider.

framework.title: Framework components
framework.body: Use createQuery for a single query with built-in tools and permissions, InteractiveSession for a full conversation, and createAgentRuntime to assemble a host runtime.

embedding.title: Servers, bots and serverless
embedding.body: Use the framework in an SSE or WebSocket server with a full event stream for each session. Resume a saved session for each bot channel, or use a stateless runtime that stores nothing.

channels.title: One agent, many channels
channels.body: TransportRegistry runs one agent definition across multiple transports. A settings file records which transports are enabled. No separate gateway process is needed.

product.title: Product composition
product.body: Build a product from a declarative profile with assembleProduct. Use the same capability packs, slash-command modules, presets, and output styles as the coding CLI.

productHost.title: Ship your own CLI product
productHost.body: Use the published CLI package while controlling your product's entry point, identity, assets, and packaging. It provides a product-bound CLI host, desktop-host helpers for Electron, and native binary builds.

analytics.title: Diagnostics, usage and evals
analytics.body: Check settings, providers, workspace trust, and plugins in one report. Summarize local token usage and cost without sending content, export metrics without conversation content, and run evaluations as code.

cliTitle: Run an agent in your terminal.
cliLead: The coding CLI is a maintained interface built on the shared framework. The same runtime supports the terminal UI, scripts, background sessions, browser GUI, and other services.

cliFlows.title: Work interactively
cliFlows.body: Start a session, choose a permission mode, or switch to a screen-reader mode.

cliFlows.title: Script a single prompt
cliFlows.body: Print mode returns an exit code your script can check. Goal runs continue working over multiple turns.

cliFlows.title: Keep sessions running
cliFlows.body: Resume earlier work, run supervised sessions in the background, and share one daemon.

cliFlows.title: Connect other interfaces and services
cliFlows.body: Open the browser GUI, accept HTTP clients with a bearer token, or act as an MCP server.

cliFlows.title: Connect to your other sessions
cliFlows.body: From a session, message other sessions, hand off a conversation, link devices, or pair a browser.

cliFlows.title: Check setup and usage
cliFlows.body: Diagnose configuration, summarize local usage, check for updates, and run evals.

safetyTitle: Decide what the agent may do.
safetyLead: Deny, ask, and allow rules are checked before the permission mode is applied. Choose a mode when you start a run or change it during the session.

safetyNotes.title: Rules take priority over modes
safetyNotes.body: An ask rule still requires approval in bypassPermissions mode. Deleting the root, home, or working directory and writing to .git or tool configuration files are never approved automatically.

safetyNotes.title: No approval response means denial
safetyNotes.body: In default mode, a request that needs approval is denied if nobody responds, unless your host provides a permission handler.

safetyNotes.title: Sandboxed shell
safetyNotes.body: Combine permission rules with the OS sandbox so an approved command still runs with limited file and network access.

safetyLink: Read the permissions and hooks guide
architectureLead: The libraries under packages/ are neutral and reusable. The CLI and apps combine them for specific purposes. Each layer depends only on the layers below it.

layers.interface: Product interface: the terminal coding assistant
layers.composition: Product composition: profiles, capability packs, commands, presets
layers.surfaces: Terminal UI and transports using the shared wire protocol
layers.runtime: Runtime: sessions, background tasks, tools, MCP client, plugins
layers.foundation: Foundation: the conversation engine and its contracts

packagesLead: Every package is published on npm under @robota-sdk/ and shares one version. Start with the smallest set your task needs.

start.title: Start here
start.body: The engine, one provider per vendor, and validated tools.

assembly.title: App assembly
assembly.body: Sessions, permissions, background work, MCP, plugins and analysis.

multiAgent.title: Multi-agent conversation
multiAgent.body: Shared transcripts for independent agents and people.

composition.title: Product composition
composition.body: Build your own product on the same runtime.

transports.title: Transports and UI
transports.body: Connect a session to a protocol or user interface.

cli.title: Agent interface
cli.body: The coding CLI, published as a self-contained bundle.

installLead: Published packages need Node.js 22.12 or later. The standalone binary needs nothing else installed.

npx.title: Run without installing
npx.body: Fetch and start the latest CLI with npx.

global.title: Install globally
global.body: Install the CLI on your PATH with npm.

binary.title: Standalone binary
binary.body: The installer picks the binary for your OS and CPU from the latest release and verifies its SHA-256 checksum. Binaries are unsigned, so macOS and Windows may warn.

sdk.title: Embed the minimal SDK
sdk.body: The engine plus one provider package. Add agent-tools when the agent calls tools.

fitTitle: Review the source and usage terms.
fitLead: The public source shows how the SDK and CLI are assembled. Start with the packages and code relevant to your task.

fitItems.title: Open source and commercial licensing
fitItems.body: The code is available under AGPL-3.0. A commercial license is also available if you need different terms. Review the license conditions for your distribution or service.

fitItems.title: Provider costs are separate
fitItems.body: The SDK and CLI do not include model inference. Hosted providers may charge for usage. Running models locally also requires compute and operating costs.

fitItems.title: First-party showcase
fitItems.body: The coding CLI is a maintained developer tool built from the public components. Explore its source and the current showcase.

visionTitle: Our agents develop and improve one another.
visionBody: This is the project's long-term goal, rather than a promised capability. Today, the SDK and coding CLI let you choose providers, tools, and host behavior explicitly. Reliable autonomous self-development still needs to be demonstrated through actual results as the system evolves.
roadmapNote: Roadmap reviewed in October 2026. Plans may change. The public beta is available now.

faqs.question: Do I need the CLI to use the SDK?
faqs.answer: No. Import the agent framework into your own Node.js host and supply a provider. The CLI is one complete interface built from the public components.

faqs.question: Will a query run without configuring a model?
faqs.answer: You need a provider endpoint and a suitable model. The local OpenAI-compatible example requires a running server with a loaded model. For a hosted provider, use its credentials and follow its terms.

faqs.question: Does the SDK persist conversations automatically?
faqs.answer: No. A createQuery call alone does not create a persistent session. Supply a session store if your host needs to save and resume conversations.

faqs.question: What should I read before enabling tools?
faqs.answer: Review workspace trust and permission modes. In default mode, unattended runs deny requests that need approval unless your host supplies a permission handler.

faqs.question: Is the beta API stable?
faqs.answer: Not yet. The packages are 3.0.0 beta releases, and the API may change before a stable release. See the changelog for upgrade notes.

closeBody: Add a query to your app or set up the coding CLI. In either case, you choose the provider and access permissions.
